coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For When Faith
Feels Thin
coverDek: Five different voices for the days doubt gets louder than belief — and what to pray when "I believe" is the whole fight.

points.hook: Lord, I'm not sure I heard You right the first time.
paragraphs: Maybe I wrote the promise down at the wrong altar. Maybe the voice I followed was my own hope talking louder than Your Spirit. I don't need a louder sign tonight — I need to remember that the gifts and the calling of God were never something You take back just because I started doubting them.
points.verseText: For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.

points.hook: A decree: the doubt lied. The Word still stands.
paragraphs: I cancel the voice that said God changed His mind about me. I cancel the lie that says the delay is a 'no' wearing a disguise. God is not a man, that He should lie, and what He spoke over my life does not expire just because I got tired of waiting on it. I stand on the Word, not on the wait.
points.verseText: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it?

points.hook: For the doubt your body carries when nothing around you has changed yet.
paragraphs: My mouth says I believe, but my shoulders are still braced for bad news, my stomach still drops when my phone lights up, my hands still shake a little when I pray the big prayer out loud. Meet me in the gap between my confession and my nerves, Lord — I believe; help the unbelief that lives in my body, not just the doubt in my mouth.
points.verseText: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

points.hook: For the doubt you've been hiding from the very people who'd pray it through with you.
paragraphs: I've sat in service with a straight face while wondering if any of this is actually working, too embarrassed to say it out loud to the family that was built to carry it with me. Let me stop performing a certainty I don't feel and start exhorting and being exhorted the way the early church actually did it — holding the confession fast together, instead of each of us pretending alone.
points.verseText: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering... not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together... but exhorting one another.

points.hook: The Father's answer to the doubt you haven't said out loud yet.
paragraphs: I know what you haven't told anyone — the quiet question underneath all your prayers, the fear that if I really saw the state of your heart I'd pull back too. I won't. Your own heart may condemn you tonight, but I am greater than your heart, and I already know everything it's accusing you of. Rest in that tonight, not in how convinced you feel.
points.verseText: For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.

cta.closingLine: If doubt has been loud lately, let's stay connected — truth gets louder the more of us are saying it out loud together.
